ops.markdown:
Solitude Peaks signed. Their marketing lead wants a joint launch **this weekend**; Wanderline's photographer is not in Leh until the 28th.

Farah, to the team:

> "THEY SAID YES. 60-day trial, signed on the spot. But Tsering — their marketing lead — wants to go live together **this weekend**. A joint announcement post, AND a 30-second teaser for their own Instagram, in English and Hindi, narrated. Our photographer isn't in Leh till the 28th. What do we even show people?"

The whole lecture sits on that gap: **the partner wants to move faster than the agency can shoot.** Three things must exist by Monday and none of them exist at all.

Shape of the deliverable: each asset comes from a different tool, then you stitch them together yourself in any editor. The stitching is not part of the lesson.

The shot with the main product or subject **dead centre and in focus**. Coca-Cola's bottle shots are the canonical example.

It is **not** an image with heroes in it — the instructor sent the class to look the term up rather than assert it, because the wrong reading changes what you ask a tool for.
